key_insight: A simple history-aware classical model outperformed several LLM approaches for predicting the next dental procedure, and adding calibrated uncertainty plus abstention made the system more decision-support ready.
clinical_relevance: For general dentistry workflows, next-step recommendations can be made more reliable by using chart history, confidence calibration, and selective abstention rather than relying on zero-shot LLM output alone.
method: Compared four classical baselines with six LLM variants for next-procedure recommendation.
Built DentaCoPilot to output top-K CDT codes, confidence labels, an abstain flag, and chart-grounded rationale.
Used split-conformal selective prediction to provide distribution-free coverage guarantees.
evidence_signal: On MEPS 2023 data (11,016 transitions from 5,088 patients), the history-aware model reached 0.479 top-1 accuracy versus 0.297 for a most-frequent baseline, with expected calibration error of 0.031.
watch_item: The stronger results come from retrospective and partly synthetic evaluation, so real-world CDT-level validation and prospective clinician testing are still needed.
paper_title: A Zero-Shot Decision Model (Jev) Matches a Trained Classifier but Ranks Its Own Errors Worse: Calibrated, Split-Conformal Next-Procedure Recommendation in General Dentistry
